ownedProcessFacade: Fixed action and service allowlists; no shell, arbitrary process IDs, URLs, credentials or headers from protocol requests.
Queued lifecycle operations with duplicate request rejection and idempotent closure.
Observed app-stop requirements retain zero exit, no forced close and writer-lock absence.
Bounded public-response fields exclude Set-Cookie and exception text; nested error codes remain visible.
independentPythonBackend: Owned relative paths and occupied rollback-target rejection.
Loads the pinned unchanged Transaction gate without constructing the operational LinuxBackend or invoking its service-control methods.
Reuses the base HTTP acceptance validation with owned request, listener and private REST adapters.
Requires actual Linux UID 996/GID 987, NoNewPrivileges, zero capabilities, loopback-only interfaces and scoped cgroup resource limits before enabling effects.
Retains 55-second forward and 120-second recovery windows, with an additional independent 90-second rehearsal budget.

tests.fixtures: synthetic in-process objects and parser inputs, not actual application processes

remaining: Implement and validate a bounded serialized subprocess transport around the owned facade.
Prepare exact reviewed old/candidate payloads, synthetic MCP-only configuration and genuine expiring native copy proof; do not invent UID, network or resource evidence.
Exercise actual Python Transaction success and fault rollback with actual owned processes and late writes in separately controlled native units.
Only after all native and deployment gates pass, seek the applicable fresh production maintenance authorization and perform final user acceptance.
limitations: This phase did not start LACK or Caddy processes.
Unit fixture observations and parser samples are not native kernel attestations.
The positive native preflight, real RPC timeout/late-response handling and real Transaction cutover/rollback are not yet tested.
Production co-host health was not probed from isolated tests; no such acceptance is claimed.
